provider: Science Data Bank (ScienceDB, Chinese Academy of Sciences / CNIC)

free_tier.stated: 1 TB per dataset and 2,000 files per dataset, with no per-user or per-account cap; the 1 TB/2,000-file line is a soft gate (contact [address removed] for more) rather than a hard refusal. 'Data packages' bundle multiple datasets under one published record.

egress.terms: Free public HTTPS download; no egress accounting in any policy page read.

tooling: Web upload plus an Open API and OAI-PMH (listed in the help centre nav). No S3 backend exposed, so bulk automation is upload-by-UI or the Open API.
chaining: Unlimited datasets x 1 TB each is the stated model; data packages then group them. This is the one Chinese academic repository that needs no +86 phone, no Alipay and no real-name verification - registration accepts username/password, GitHub, ORCID or WeChat, and only the first two are needed.
limits_note: Review gate before publication; upload UI is the practical path (no public write API found for bulk); 2,000-file soft cap per dataset.

evidence.proved: 'if a single dataset contains more than 2,000 files or exceeds 1 TB in size, file upload functionality will be restricted... contact the ScienceDB official email'
registration 'using the username and password you created during registration, or through third-party authentication such as CAS email/CSD account, GitHub account, ORCID and WeChat account'
comparative table: ScienceDB 'no limit on data volume, users can upload datasets of any size' vs Zenodo 50 GB

binding_note: the write is a queue with a person or a rule in it, so the upload rate is set by somebody else
